chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ، الْأَرْمَنِيُّ. ضَعِيفٌ، مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ. يُقَالُ: رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: ʿAbdullāh b. al-Ḥakam, al-Armanī. Weak, a proponent of irtifāʿ in doctrine. It is said: he narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥakam al-Armanī as a weak narrator who transmitted from Imam al-Sadiq (AS). His specific defect, *irtifāʿ al-qawl* (elevating speech), suggests a tendency toward exaggeration regarding the Imams' status, a trait often linked to the *Ghulat* sects, which distinguishes his narrations within the broader context of Shia hadith criticism.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥakam al-Armanī and what does 'irtifāʿ al-qawl' mean in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (in terms of hadith narrator reliability)
key_terms.مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ: Proponent of irtifāʿ (elevating the status/rank of the Imams)
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
